name: Koch network

summary.text: The Koch network refers to Koch Industries, a privately held conglomerate in Wichita, Kansas, led by chairman and co-CEO Charles Koch, together with the Koch family foundations and the advocacy groups they fund, principally Americans for Prosperity, founded by David Koch (Greenpeace dates it to 2004 with an $850,000 seed grant; DeSmog reports it replaced the Citizens for a Sound Economy Foundation). Greenpeace's tally of IRS filings puts Koch foundation giving to 90 groups that opposed climate science or policy at about $145.5 million from 1997 to 2018. A 2013 peer-reviewed study by Robert Brulle found Koch-affiliated foundations and the ExxonMobil Foundation heavily involved in funding climate counter-movement groups from 2003 to 2007, with no publicly traceable contributions after 2008. In June 2020 the Minnesota Attorney General sued Koch Industries, ExxonMobil and the American Petroleum Institute alleging consumer fraud over climate change; the allegations have not been decided.

facts.claim: Koch Industries is a privately held company headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, described as the second-largest private company in the United States after Cargill, with Charles Koch as chairman and co-CEO. Its holdings include Flint Hills Resources, Georgia-Pacific, Guardian Industries, Infor, Invista, Koch Minerals & Trading and Molex. Because the company is private, published revenue figures are estimates.
facts.quote: Koch is the second-largest private company in the U.S., behind Cargill, and is headquartered in Wichita, Kansas. Charles Koch serves as chairman and co-CEO.

sources.title: Koch Industries Inc. – Company History
Flint Hills Resources

facts.claim: Greenpeace USA, working from the Koch family foundations' IRS Form 990 filings, reports that those foundations gave $145,555,197 between 1997 and 2018 to 90 groups that attacked climate change science and policy solutions. Greenpeace is an advocacy organisation and applies a broad definition of what counts as obstructing climate policy.
facts.quote: Koch Family Foundations have spent $145,555,197 directly financing 90 groups that have attacked climate change science and policy solutions, from 1997-2018.

sources.title: Koch Industries: Secretly Funding the Climate Denial Machine

facts.claim: Americans for Prosperity was founded by David Koch of Koch Industries. Greenpeace reports it was founded in 2004 with an undisclosed $850,000 seed grant from David Koch, making him its largest initial donor, and that AFP received about $6.3 million from Koch foundations between 2005 and 2017. DeSmog dates the organisation's establishment to 2003, when it replaced the Citizens for a Sound Economy Foundation.
facts.quote: Greenpeace says AFP was founded in 2004 with an undisclosed $850,000 seed grant from David Koch, making him the largest initial donor.

sources.title: Americans for Prosperity Foundation (AFP)
Americans for Prosperity
Americans for Prosperity – research and background information

facts.claim: In 2008, a year after the Supreme Court ruled that the EPA could regulate greenhouse gases, Americans for Prosperity devised the 'No Climate Tax' pledge, under which signers promise to oppose any climate legislation that includes a net increase in government revenue. The Tax Policy Center estimated signers at about 140 House members, 26 senators and 8 governors; in November 2012 AFP said House Republican leaders John Boehner, Eric Cantor and Kevin McCarthy had signed.
facts.quote: The pledge's wording is that signers will oppose any legislation relating to climate change that includes a net increase in government revenue.

sources.title: Tax Pledge Adds Another Political Hurdle to U.S. Climate Action
What's the No Climate Tax Pledge?
House GOP leadership pledged to oppose climate tax

facts.claim: Robert Brulle's 2013 study in Climatic Change, using IRS and Foundation Center data for 2003 to 2010 on 91 climate counter-movement organisations funded by 140 foundations, found that Koch-affiliated foundations and the ExxonMobil Foundation were heavily involved in funding such organisations from 2003 to 2007 but made no publicly traceable contributions after 2008, while the donor-directed fund Donors Trust grew to about 25% of identifiable funding from about 3% in 2003.
facts.quote: from 2003 to 2007, the Koch Affiliated Foundations and the ExxonMobil Foundation were heavily involved in funding climate-change denial organizations. But since 2008, they are no longer making publicly traceable contributions.

sources.title: Institutionalizing delay: foundation funding and the creation of U.S. climate change counter-movement organizations
Not just the Koch brothers: New study reveals funders behind the climate change denial effort

facts.claim: On 24 June 2020 Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison sued ExxonMobil, Koch Industries (with its subsidiaries Flint Hills Resources LP and Flint Hills Resources Pine Bend) and the American Petroleum Institute in Ramsey County District Court, alleging violations of the state's consumer fraud, deceptive trade practices and failure-to-warn laws through a decades-long campaign of misleading statements about climate change. The state seeks restitution, a corrective public education campaign and an injunction. The claims are allegations that have not been decided.
facts.quote: Minnesota's Attorney General sued ExxonMobil, Koch Industries and the American Petroleum Institute in June 2020 in Ramsey County, alleging violations of state and common law regarding consumer fraud, deceptive trade practices, misrepresentation, failure to warn.

sources.title: Attorney General Ellison sues ExxonMobil, Koch Industries and American Petroleum Institute
Minnesota sues oil companies, institute over climate change

facts.claim: Koch Industries' public affairs executive Mike Morgan has held a seat on the American Legislative Exchange Council's corporate 'Private Enterprise' board since at least the late 1990s and previously chaired it. The Center for Media and Democracy reported that Koch Industries gave ALEC $504,700 between 1995 and 1998, and that Charles Koch gave just over $2 million to ALEC between 2017 and 2021 through his foundation and Stand Together Fellowships.
facts.quote: Koch Industries' Mike Morgan has had a place on ALEC's corporate "Private Enterprise" board (which it now calls an "advisory council") since at least the late 1990s, and previously chaired ALEC's corporate board that meets jointly with its legislative board.

connections.claim: Koch Industries funds ALEC through membership dues and sponsorship fees and holds a seat on its corporate board through executive Mike Morgan; Koch family foundations have also given directly, including just over $2 million from Charles Koch's foundation and Stand Together Fellowships between 2017 and 2021.
connections.quote: Koch funds ALEC, both through the membership dues and sponsorship fees paid by Koch Industries, and through direct contributions from Koch family foundations.

connections.quote: Americans for Prosperity was founded by David H. Koch of Koch Industries.

connections.claim: Brulle's 2013 study found that Koch-affiliated foundations stopped making publicly traceable contributions to climate counter-movement groups after 2008, while the donor-directed fund Donors Trust rose to about 25% of identifiable funding to such groups; the Center for Media and Democracy describes DonorsTrust as the preferred donor conduit of the Koch political network. The study did not trace specific Koch money through Donors Trust.
connections.quote: Donors Trust is the central example. Brulle describes it as a "black box," and it now makes up about 25% of funding for organizations engaged in climate denial efforts, up from just three percent in 2003.

sources.title: Study Details Dark Money Flowing to Climate Science Denial

connections.quote: The lawsuit names Koch subsidiaries Flint Hills Resources LP and Flint Hills Resources Pine Bend as defendants, alongside the parent company.

openQuestions: Koch foundation grants to the Heritage Foundation could not be sourced to a specific figure; the foundations' 990-PF filings (Part XV) would show them.

The Center for Climate Integrity reported in May 2026 that the Minnesota Supreme Court allowed the state's case to proceed and that the U.S. Department of Justice then sued Minnesota; this comes from an advocacy group and should be checked against the court docket.
Greenpeace's $145.5 million figure is an advocacy tally from tax filings; a separate Greenpeace page gives $127 million to 92 groups for 1997-2017.
Revenue figures for Koch Industries vary by source and are estimates; the company does not publish them.
Charles G. Koch Foundation funding of Willie Soon is already recorded in the API findings and was not repeated here.

A concurrent draft of this file carried summary text on Americans for Prosperity's 2004 split from Citizens for a Sound Economy, a Forbes-based 2019 revenue estimate of $115 billion, and 2010 reporting linking AFP to Tea Party organising (the Manufacturing Consent page). Those statements had no matching sources in the file and were removed from the summary; the owner may wish to merge them from that draft's sources.
